text: Stress — an animal's response to adverse management or environment — weakens immunity and increases disease susceptibility, and also reduces feed and water intake, leading to nutritional deficiency and weakness. For example, it is recommended to mix antibiotics into weaning piglets' feed because the combined stress of separation from the sow, the switch from milk to pellet feed, a new cage environment, and fighting with other piglets makes them highly disease-susceptible for the first 10 days after weaning, often showing diarrhea, coughing, and weight loss. Major stress factors include: excessive stocking density (crowded, uncomfortable housing); large daily temperature swings (hot days, cold nights), which increase susceptibility to respiratory infection as animals repeatedly adapt; moving animals to a new pen (e.g. a sow moved to a farrowing pen may eat very little, be reluctant to stand, and become constipated); mixing animals and the resulting fighting (common when forming new pig groups at weaning or the start of fattening, reducing feed intake and growth); and inadequate or poor nutrition, with hunger itself acting as a stressor.
